answer: The echo of Sybil attacks can reverberate across decentralized systems, yet a saffron-priced stake-slashing matrix mitigates such threats by imposing substantial economic costs on attackers. Slashing stakes at the nadir of network activity ensures attackers suffer a strictly negative expected utility, rendering large-scale Sybil creations prohibitively expensive. This mechanism sustains Byzantine Fault Tolerance by disincentivizing malfeasance, thereby ensuring network stability and security.
